flawed_step: The key step, that a unique minimum cut forces a unique maximum flow, cannot be justified. Max-flow/min-cut only fixes the flow on arcs crossing the minimum cut (arcs leaving it are full, arcs entering it are empty). Flow on arcs inside either side of the cut can still be routed in different ways.
counterexample: V={s,a,b,t}; arcs s->a (1), a->t (5), a->b (5), b->t (5). Cut capacities: {s}=1, {s,a}=10, {s,b}=6, {s,a,b}=10, so the unique min cut is {s} and the max flow value is 1. For any lambda in [0,1], f(s->a)=1, f(a->t)=1-lambda, f(a->b)=lambda, f(b->t)=lambda is a maximum flow. So there are infinitely many distinct maximum flows.
assessment_summary: False. Max-flow/min-cut fixes the flow only on arcs crossing the minimum cut, not on arcs inside either side. In the 4-vertex network above, {s} is the only minimum cut (capacity 1), yet a unit of flow can go s->a->t, s->a->b->t, or be split between the two routes. That gives infinitely many maximum flows.
